samples.summary: 'does not split a band at a zero-width soft line break' passes whether or not the \n skip exists — it is insensitive to the behaviour it claims to guard
samples.evidence: The test only asserts `rects.length === lines.length`. layout.ts:928-942 appends the '\n' segment with width 0 and the SAME inline style at the END of the line before flushing, so in drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLine (paint-layout.ts:260-276) that run resolves to the same colour and sets `right = lineX + run.x + 0`, equal to the previous run's right edge. Deleting `if (run.text === '\n') continue;` therefore still yields exactly one band per line and the assertion stays green. The test asserts no geometry (no x/width) and does not pin `lines.length > 1`, so both sides of the equality are computed rather than expected.

samples.summary: renderRun's changed per-run background rect (`bgRight - x`), the header/footer path, has no test
samples.evidence: paint-layout.ts:481-495 now rounds both edges of the per-run bg fillRect. The only caller reaching this branch is doc-canvas.ts:721-725 (renderRunWithPageNumber, skipBackground: false). No test asserts a fillRect emitted by renderRun: every renderRun call in paint-layout.test.ts uses makeBaselineCtx / makeStrokeCtx / makeFillStyleCtx, all of which stub fillRect as a no-op (test lines 41, 102, 180). A wrong width would ship as a visible header/footer highlight seam or overhang with a green suite.
searchedFor: grep renderRun call sites in packages/*/src and packages/docs/test
read all ctx stubs in paint-layout.test.ts (fillRect: noop)

samples.summary: drawInlineRunBackgroundsForPage — the DocCanvas body path where issue #1036 is reported — has no test of its own
samples.evidence: DocCanvas paints body highlights via drawInlineRunBackgroundsForPage (doc-canvas.ts:416) and passes skipRunBackgrounds: true, so none of the new tests (which call paintLayout with default opts, exercising drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLayout) cover it. A repo-wide grep for drawInlineRunBackgrounds matches only src files plus table-renderer.test.ts; nothing asserts the page-shaped wrapper's `pageX + pl.x` / `pageY + pl.y` mapping or its table/hr/page-break skip, so a glue mistake would leave the user-visible bug unfixed undetected.

samples.summary: Table-cell call site is covered only by a single-run, integer-coordinate fixture, so neither coalescing nor the newly introduced rounding is exercised
samples.evidence: table-renderer.test.ts:247-257 uses makeTableWithInlineBg() with exactly one run (x: 0, width: 20) at padding 4 and asserts fillRect(4, 4, 20, 16). The old code passed unrounded `cellX + padding + run.x`; the new code rounds both edges, and the fixture's coordinates are integers, so the assertion holds either way. No table fixture has two adjacent runs or fractional x/width, so a coalescing or rounding regression inside cells would not be caught.

samples.summary: Documented band-breaking cases other than 'no backgroundColor' are untested: image runs and unresolvable colours
samples.evidence: drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLine (paint-layout.ts:263-269) newly treats style.image and a falsy resolver result (including the `|| undefined` coercion of an empty string) as band terminators, and the JSDoc at 231-235 states this as contract. The new describe block only covers an un-highlighted run (test line 434); no test passes an image inline or a custom colorResolver returning ''/undefined. Failure mode: an image gets an unwanted fill, or a highlight merges across an image.
searchedFor: read the whole new describe block in paint-layout.test.ts (lines 375-443)
grep colorResolver and style.image in packages/docs/test

samples.summary: No test pins the new invariant that paintLayout emits zero run-background fills when skipRunBackgrounds is true
samples.evidence: paintBlock now hardcodes `skipBackground: true` (paint-layout.ts:189) and the option doc at 50-57 states the caller's pass is then the ONLY painter. All new tests call `paintLayout(ctx, layout, 0, 0)` with default opts (test line 367), so the DocCanvas configuration is never painted in a test; nothing would fail if that branch regressed to painting per-run rects on top of DocCanvas's bands — the exact re-banding the new comment warns about.
